assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, with Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstrations of record accuracy and stability, extended time and frequency metrology by orders of magnitude. This is the kind of new measurement capability I value most: it opened relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and the road to a redefinition of the second. The idea was original, the experimental execution is exacting and the impact reaches far beyond atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the magic-wavelength proposal and early Sr lattice-clock work; Ye's JILA group delivered the decisive accuracy and coherence demonstrations. A two-person prize is clean and fair. Other contributors (e.g. Lemonde, Takamoto, ion-clock groups) sit outside the supplied credit, so the allocation is workable but not exhaustive.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent clocks at NIST, PTB, SYRTE, RIKEN and elsewhere, with accuracy at the 1e-18 level. The field has matured and the recognition is timely, as the SI second redefinition is under active discussion.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views clocks as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 frequency comb and 2012 ion-control prizes.
Some credit boundaries relative to ion clocks and comb work are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics turned superconducting circuits into controllable, readable qubits coupled to resonators. It is the architecture behind most current superconducting quantum processors, and the dispersive readout and strong-coupling demonstrations are clean experiments with long-lasting engineering impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais (theory with Girvin and colleagues), Wallraff (first strong coupling with Schoelkopf's group) and Schoelkopf (transmon, readout, bosonic codes) form a coherent trio. Girvin and Devoret/Yale co-contributors are not among the credited names. Devoret's 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling is related but distinct.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed by many independent groups and industrial platforms. Recognition is timely, though the recent 2025 prize in superconducting circuits may make the committee cautious about adjacency.
uncertainties: Credit split between theory proposal and experiment is debatable, and uncredited key people (e.g. Girvin, Devoret) are omitted from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical initialization, coherent control and readout of single NV and related defect spins is a measurement technology with wide reach: nanoscale magnetometry, biological sensing, quantum networks and loophole-free Bell tests. The coherence times and room-temperature operation are what experimentalists care about.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup first showed optical detection of single NV spins, Awschalom developed coherent control and defect platforms broadly, and Hanson pushed spin-photon entanglement and network nodes. Lukin and Walsworth also made major contributions, so the three-name limit is a real constraint. I propose the three most foundational names.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations and commercial sensors exist. The sensing side is mature, while the networks side is still developing.
uncertainties: Three-laureate cap forces exclusion of Lukin, Walsworth, Jelezko-type contributors.
A compound field of sensing and networking that may need different framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry provided inertial sensors, gravimeters and precision tests of fundamental physics with matter waves. From my viewpoint it is a prime example of how a new measurement principle opens fields such as gravimetry and tests of equivalence principle and constants.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard did early atom-optics and interferometer work, Bordé provided the theory and Ramsey-Bordé interferometry, and Kasevich with Chu made the first inertial sensing demonstrations. Chu's 1997 prize covers laser cooling, which affects attribution framing. Müller is later work. Allocation among four is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Technique is well established, with commercial gravimeters and large-scale experiments in progress. Some headline applications (long-baseline gravitational wave detection, equivalence tests) remain in development.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior cooling prizes and with Chu's contributions.
Fair division of credit among four candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed-light injection beats the standard quantum limit in interferometers and is now routine in LIGO and Virgo, a concrete case of quantum physics improving a flagship instrument. The idea by Caves was foundational, and the engineering was demanding.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the theoretical proposal, Schnabel and Mavalvala led key implementations in GEO600 and LIGO, and Kimble's group and Slusher's 1985 squeezing experiments also matter. The earliest experimental squeezing credit is outside my three chosen names and complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: Operational in GEO600 and LIGO with demonstrated sensitivity improvements, so it is well confirmed and mature. The 2017 prize on LIGO partly covers the setting.
uncertainties: Early experimental squeezing credit (Slusher, Kimble, Wu) is complicated.
Possible overlap with the 2017 gravitational-wave prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models with tunable parameters and single-site readout, enabling quantum simulation of many-body physics. The experimental control and microscopy are impressive, and the field has had wide influence on condensed matter and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch demonstrated the Mott insulator transition and quantum gas microscopy, and Esslinger realized fermionic Hubbard physics. Zoller and Cirac supplied the foundational theory; the five-name list exceeds three laureates, so selection is a real compromise.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups, with maturing quantitative results on Fermi-Hubbard physics. Remaining scientific questions (e.g. d-wave pairing) are still open, but the platform is established.
uncertainties: Five credited names versus a three-person limit; theory credit to Zoller and Cirac is omitted from my proposal.
Overlap with earlier Bose-Einstein condensation prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg-blockade tweezer arrays enable programmable quantum simulators and emerging neutral-atom computers, with demonstrated entanglement and arrays of hundreds of atoms. It is a very active, high-impact area building on strong experimental demonstrations.
assessment.attribution: Saffman contributed key gate proposals, Browaeys showed blockade between single atoms and spin models, and Lukin led large-scale programmable arrays. Others (Weiss, Bernien and Endres, Regal, Ahn) are also important and unresolved in allocation.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly developing, with independent groups and companies now reproducing the results. Interpretation of quantum advantage and error rates is still evolving, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Maturity: the field is still evolving, and fidelity benchmarks are improving.
Attribution among many tweezer groups is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coherent interfaces between light and matter (cavity QED nodes, quantum memories, EIT-based storage) underpin quantum networks and repeaters. This is close to my own field of work, so I know that demonstrations here are experimentally hard, with efficiency, storage time and fidelity as the decisive figures of merit.
assessment.attribution: Kimble proposed and demonstrated the quantum internet concept, Rempe built single-atom cavity-QED nodes, and Lukin contributed EIT-based storage and protocols. Rare-earth and atomic-ensemble memory groups are not covered by the credited names, so the credited configuration captures only part of the field.
assessment.maturity: Proofs of principle are established, but practical networks with useful rates over long distances remain to be shown, so recognition may be premature relative to other candidates.
uncertainties: Practical repeater performance is not yet demonstrated.
Disclosure: I work in a related field, and I may be biased in weighting memory work.
